question: Can the existing full-eye measured-grid sensory interface be made numerically convergent under the exact same biological and scene assumptions?
public_scope: Canonical scientific record. All material assumptions, methods, failures, corrections, diagnostics, provenance, and exact raw archive access needed to evaluate this result are included here or in the public CNS release asset.

frozen_method.optical: Integrate the identical normalized exp(-theta^2/(2 sigma^2)) sin(theta) integral on 0..3sigma. Analytically split radial intervals at spherical-blocker tangencies and integrate only the visible azimuthal arc; add blocked constant radiance by its angular measure. Sine-squared radial mapping resolves endpoint square-root behavior. No scene smoothing or acceptance change.
frozen_method.quadrature_normalization: Use one finite full-cone normalization per numerical order, exactly once for the complete truncated spherical-Gaussian cone. Clear, mixed, and fully blocked visibility pieces are subdivisions of that same integral; never renormalize a visibility piece. Report finite full-cone mass error against a high-order direct reference separately from numerator and final normalized-light errors.

This evaluates the identical frozen normalized optical integral while removing the failed approximation. Preserve the exact Z-rotation harmonic path for nontranslation conditions.
